headline: Neighbors trust Joel. A couple of doors online are stuck.
summary: Maxx Pest Management is a family-owned pest control service out of Alpine, handling common household pests along with rats and mice, gopher treatment and humane wildlife trapping. Neighbors on Nextdoor named it a Neighborhood Favorite in 2024 and 2025 and describe Joel as very knowledgeable, professional and kind, which is exactly the reputation a small pest company wants. The phone number is the same on the website and Nextdoor, the website clearly explains what you do, and your Google listing is up with the website and phone linked. The leftover that still hurts is the Contact email on the site: the address printed there has a small spelling slip in the part after the @, and that address can't receive mail, so anyone who writes to you from the site is likely never reaching you. The correct Gmail address is already on Nextdoor, so this is a quick copy-and-paste fix. A couple of small website touch-ups, like replacing a leftover sample quote and naming the towns you serve, would round it out.

signals.note: Your Google listing is up as Maxx Pest Management, marked open, with maxxpestmanagement.com and (619) 212-1595. People searching pest control around Alpine can land on you. Your Nextdoor reputation is strong, so keeping the Google profile matched keeps that word of mouth easy to find.
signals.next: Keep the Google hours and phone matched to whatever you post on the site and Nextdoor once those go up. After any change, ask a few happy customers to leave a review.

signals.note: Your number, (619) 212-1595, is the same on your website and on Nextdoor, so callers reach the right place. That's the most important door, and it's working. Keep it identical on Google too.
signals.next: Use (619) 212-1595 exactly as-is on the Google profile. If you ever add a text line or a second number, list it as additional rather than swapping this one out.

signals.note: We didn't find business hours posted on your website or your Nextdoor page. Google currently shows Monday to Friday 8 to 6, weekends closed. Customers often check hours before calling to see whether they'll get a person or voicemail. Even rough hours on the site help set expectations.
signals.next: Add your usual working hours to the website footer and to Nextdoor, and use the same hours on the Google profile. If you work by appointment, say so in one short line.

signals.note: The Google listing is live, so there's already a place on Maps for people to see your truck, your gear or you on the job. Photos are a big part of why people pick one small pest company over another. They help a new customer feel like they know who's coming to the door.
signals.next: Add a handful of real photos to the profile: the truck, Joel on a job, a set trap or a gopher treatment. A new photo every month or two keeps the listing fresh.

signals.note: maxxpestmanagement.com explains your services well and names Joel. The email in the Contact section has a spelling slip in the domain, and that domain doesn't accept mail, so notes sent from the site can't reach you. The About section also still shows a sample quote from the website template credited to a placeholder name.
signals.next: Change the Contact email to the same Gmail address that's on your Nextdoor page, then send yourself a test note from the site to be sure it arrives. Swap the sample quote for a real line from a customer, with their permission.

signals.note: Nextdoor lists you in Alpine, while the website just says San Diego Area. Your phone matches in both places and on Google, but the email addresses differ because of the site's spelling slip. Search engines trust a business more when the name, town, phone and email line up everywhere.
signals.next: Name Alpine and the nearby towns you serve on the website, and use the same email on the site, Nextdoor and Google. A quick check of both pages after the change keeps them matched.
